saints.name: St. Marcellus I
saints.title: Pope and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: The pope who rebuilt the Roman Church after the great persecution and was exiled for his firmness with the lapsed…
biography: Marcellus was elected bishop of Rome in May 308, after the see had stood vacant nearly four years through the persecution of Diocletian. He found the Church in disorder, its meeting-places confiscated and great numbers of the faithful fallen away under the terror.

To rebuild, he divided Rome into twenty-five districts, the tituli, each under a priest charged with baptism, public penance, the burial of the dead, and the commemorations of the martyrs, and he laid out a new cemetery on the Via Salaria. His demand that the lapsed do penance before readmission broke into open riot, which Pope Damasus later recalled in verses cut above his grave.

Maxentius, master of Rome, had him seized and banished at the end of 308, and Marcellus died in exile on 16 January 309, after a reign of little more than a year and a half. A later legend made him die a groom in the imperial horse-post; the Church has honored him as a martyr for her discipline, and his relics rest under the altar of San Marcello al Corso.
saints.knownFor: Restoring order to the Church of Rome after persecution.
